newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek bonds pare losses, ecu/drachma well bid.
newsitem.headline: Greek bonds pare losses, ecu/drachma well bid.

text.p: Greek bonds recovered early morning losses in late dealings, forex forwards were steady to lower, depos were softer and ecu/drachma was well bid above 312, traders said.

"The market is quiet but nervous with bonds having pared early losses after the finance ministry announced the auction sums for bonds in June," a dealer at a foreign bank said. "This removed a source of uncertainty and helped prices."
The finance ministry said it would auction 100 billion drachmas of 10-year, fixed coupon bonds and re-open bids for 50 billion drachmas each of three-, five- and seven-year bonds on June 17.
The treasury will issue 12-month T-bills at 9.60 percent on June 2, down 10 basis points, reopen bids for three-, five- and seven-year coupon bonds and auction 10-year fixed coupon bonds on June 19.
Greece auctioned three-year, 9.80 percent bonds, five-year, 9.20 percent bonds and seven-year, 8.9 percent bonds on March 19.
"We are still monitoring what happens at the fixing and ecu/drachma," said another bond trader. "There is still plenty of tension around with forex and money markets in bad shape lately."

The drachma continued to be weak against the ecu, oscillating in the 312.0/40 band forcing the central bank to intervene and sell 200 million ecus and 25 million marks for drachmas at the fixing to support the local currency.

"The central bank wants to support the drachma but today's intervention was not as aggressive as I expected it to be," said a forex dealer at a foreign bank. "It should not let the mark rise to 160.135 given the small amounts involved."
But other dealers expressed satisfaction with the central bank's stance to back up the drachma.
"The central bank did its deed," said a forex dealer at a private bank.
The central bank sold 350 million ecus and 80 million marks on Tuesday.
"Depos are trading lower in late dealings but forex forwards except for one-year tenors which trade lower are stable," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
"Forex outflows and their impact on liquidity is of primary importance to the market," said a dealer at another bank.
The mark was quoted at 160.27/37 from Wednesday's 160.135 fix, the dollar at 272.72/82 drachmas from 272.22 and the ecu at 312.11/21 from 311.950 drachmas.
The National Bank of Greece, the domestic money market's biggest player, quoted the following late rates:
** Overnight at 9.80-10.30
** One week at 10.20-10.70
** Two weeks at 10.20-10.70
** Three weeks at 10.20-10.70
** One month at 10.20-10.70
** Two months at 10.20-10.70
** Three months at 10.10-10.60
** Six months at 9.90-10.40
** Nine months at 9.85-10.35
** Twelve months at 9.80-10.30
--Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
